reason: A cue/reference contrast can unlock a generic function of RGB features merely through a recognizable view type. A fair RGB capacity control must retain that ability even when its two physical foreground views coincide.
RGB_control: Keep the second ordinary RGB bounding-box ownership/unmasked-crop view, and add a fixed+0.25 marker to its final cue channel before shared Train-only normalization. The marker contains no identity, scene or IR information.
IR_method: Use actual new-IR cue values, with no extra constant marker; unavailable IR gives exact zero increment as registered
reference: Keep the RGB-reference vector unchanged for both heads
architecture_and_budget: Identical40-input shared network, bounded contrast, seeds, row draws, epochs and optimizer; marker adds no parameters
required_interventions: If the full method improves, test removal/misalignment of IR values as well as the trained RGB capacity control; an auxiliary type tag or generic extra capacity is not proof of IR information.
